meta.homeDescription: A free test that places you on twelve political axes and shows which ideologies, countries, figures and parties sit closest, with honest uncertainty. No account needed.

footer.disclaimer: Spectrum is an interpretation tool. It reads your answers through a model with real limits; it does not measure who you are.
footer.privacy: Your answers stay in your browser unless you choose to save them.

home.sentence: Twelve axes, because politics doesn’t fit on one line.

quick.name: Quick
quick.blurb: A first sketch of where you stand.

standard.name: Standard
standard.blurb: A sharper picture with sturdier confidence.

deep.name: Deep
deep.blurb: The most detailed reading: twelve questions per axis.

home.modesNote: You can extend a shorter test later and keep your answers. What you see here is the whole test: no hidden extra rounds.
home.kicker: Spectrum · a twelve-axis political test · free · no account
home.subline: Answer short statements and see where you stand, which ideologies sit closest, and how sure that picture is.

field.description: {count} ideologies from the catalog placed on the overall map, the first two principal components of all twelve axes. Bigger halftone dots mean more ideologies nearby; each marker shows its spectrum by shape.
field.caption: Fig. 01 — Catalog, {count} entries
field.keyboard: Catalog map. Arrow keys step through the ideologies, Enter jumps to the index entry.

answer.title: Answer
answer.body: React to plain statements on a five-point scale. Not sure? Skip it. A skip is not counted as neutral.

see.body: Each axis gets a score and a confidence. Where your answers pull in different directions, the results say so.

explore.title: Explore and track
explore.body: Compare yourself with ideologies, countries, figures and parties, and see how your views move over time.

axes.title: Twelve independent axes
axes.lead: Each axis is measured on its own. During the test you never see which axis a statement belongs to; that is revealed with your results.

index.title: Index of ideologies
index.lead: All {count} entries in the catalog so far, A to Z, each with its spectrum. Full pages arrive with the catalog.

privacy.statement: Your answers stay in your browser.

results.title: Your results

sharedResult.brokenBody: The code is incomplete or was changed, so it cannot be read. Ask for the link again, or take the test yourself.
sharedResult.yourTurn: Where do you stand? The test takes 5 to 10 minutes and needs no account.

dashboard.title: Your dashboard
dashboard.lead: Every result you take is kept in this browser, so you can see how your views change over time.

compass.title: Compass
compass.lead: A continuous map of the political space: pick any two axes, or the overall map.

web.title: Ideology web
web.lead: Ideologies linked by similarity, grouped by family.

sandbox.title: Sandbox
sandbox.lead: Move twelve sliders and watch the closest matches change.

ideologies.title: Ideologies
ideologies.lead: Hundreds of political ideologies and traditions, from mainstream to fringe, each with criticisms and sources.

countries.title: Countries and regimes
countries.lead: Modern countries and historical regimes, each placed as of a stated date.

figures.title: Figures
figures.lead: Historical and contemporary political figures. Positions of living people are editorial estimates.

parties.title: Parties
parties.lead: Real political parties with an “as of” date and the ideologies they draw on.

method.title: Method
method.lead: How answers become scores, how matches are calculated, and where the model’s limits are.
method.axesLead: Each axis is independent. You can favour markets and open borders, or collective ownership and tradition. During the test you never see which axis a statement belongs to; that is revealed with your results.

answer.title: Answer
answer.body: React to plain statements on a five-point scale. Not sure? Skip it. A skip is not counted as neutral.

see.title: See twelve positions
see.body: Each axis gets a score and a confidence. Where your answers pull in different directions, the results say so.

explore.title: Explore and track
explore.body: Compare yourself with ideologies, countries, figures and parties, and see how your views move over time.

local.title: Local-first
local.body: Results are saved in your browser. Nothing reaches a server unless you choose encrypted sync.

tracking.title: No tracking
tracking.body: No ads, no analytics, no third-party scripts. No cookies unless you create a profile.

honest.title: Honest uncertainty
honest.body: Matches are spread out, not inflated, and every result shows how confident it is.

neutral.title: Even-handed catalog
neutral.body: Every ideology, mainstream or fringe, gets the same encyclopedic treatment, criticisms included.

privacy.title: Privacy
privacy.lead: Political views are sensitive. This page explains, in plain words, what is stored, where and for how long.
privacy.now: Today: this site sets no cookies, runs no analytics and stores nothing on a server.

imprint.title: Imprint
imprint.pending: The responsible party will be named here before public launch.

notFound.title: This page doesn’t exist
notFound.body: The address may be mistyped, or the page may have moved.

styleguide.title: Styleguide
styleguide.lead: Every component and state in both modes, for design review. Hover states are also shown pinned, so they can be checked without a pointer.

palette.note: Two colours, swapped between modes. No greys, accents, gradients, shadows, opacity, blur or rounded corners. A CI check rejects any other colour.

type.mono: Interface, labels and numbers: IBM Plex Mono
type.sampleHeadline: Where would you draw the line?
type.sampleBody: Each axis is measured on its own. A position on one says nothing about the others, which is exactly why twelve lines describe a person better than one.

buttons.note: Hover wipes the opposite colour in from the left while the label flips with it; the arrow rolls. Press scales to 98% and springs back. Focus is a 2px ring at 3px. Disabled is dashed.

inputs.note: Labels sit above fields. Errors are written out and thicken the frame; colour never carries meaning.
inputs.error: Error: type at least two letters.
inputs.consent: I understand that this file contains my political views.

answer.note: Full-width rows. Pressing wipes the row in; the chosen row stays inverted and its [X] draws in. Keycaps 1–5 show on desktop. With auto-advance on, the test waits 180ms so the choice registers.

cells.note: Structure uses 2px rules, dense data 1px. Sections are cells on a 12-column grid; tables are ruled, numbers right-aligned in tabular figures, countries as ISO codes.
cells.cellBody: Content sits in ruled cells instead of floating cards.

nav.note: Hover draws an underline; the current section has a bar that slides when the route changes, plus brackets. On phones the menu opens as a full-screen inverted sheet in display type.
nav.panelRadar: All twelve axes in one shape.
nav.panelMap: The overall map of the political space.
nav.sheet: Try the mobile sheet by narrowing the window and pressing MENU; it works without JavaScript.

sliders.note: Black bars on ruled tracks with ticks every 10 points; uncertainty as a hairline bracket or a hatched band. The slider thumb grows while dragged and a bordered readout follows it.

overlays.note: The tooltip opens after 300ms of hover, at once on focus or tap, and comes in over 120ms. The modal is a native dialog over a halftone screen; Escape closes it.
overlays.modalBody: Overlays have a 2px frame and no shadow. The page behind is covered by a dot screen instead of being dimmed or blurred.

legend.note: Every encoding has a written key. Spectra are told apart by shape plus code, never by shape alone.
legend.solid: Solid line: you, or the first series
legend.dotted: Sparse dots: older steps of your trail
legend.halftone: Halftone: bigger dots, more ideologies nearby
legend.you: You: the circle’s size shows uncertainty, the crosshair marks the point
legend.ghost: Ghost compare: a hollow, dashed outline
legend.dither: Ordered dither: the band under the sticky header

strip.note: Twelve two-letter axis codes, grouped by domain.
strip.how: Each code has four squares: the left two belong to the first pole, the right two to the second. One filled square means the entry leans that way, two mean it leans strongly, none means it sits near the centre.

radar.note: Centre = −100, solid inner ring = 0, outer ring = +100 on every axis. First profile: solid line, hatched fill, solid corners. Comparison: dashed line, empty fill, hollow corners.
radar.title: Radar: example profile A against B

compass.note: Static preview of the Phase 4 compass on the anchor catalog: distribution across, state power up.
compass.title: Compass preview: distribution and state power
compass.summary: Halftone dots show where ideologies cluster. One marker per spectrum, your position with its uncertainty circle, three earlier results as a trail, and a friend as a ghost.

web.note: Static preview of the Phase 10 web view: placement from the overall map, each node joined to its two nearest neighbours. Hover over a node to see its name.
web.title: Web view preview: seventeen anchor ideologies

images.note: Photos become 1-bit ordered-dither images at build time. Author, licence and source stay visible under every image.
images.glyphsNote: Each catalog entry gets a symmetric 5×5 pattern derived from its id: original, no symbols, no faces.
images.flagsNote: No flags. Countries are named and coded in text, e.g. CH, DE, FR.

controls.label: Control style
controls.note: The control style applies to the whole site and is remembered in this browser, for review only. Sharp is the default until a choice is made.

links.note: Links are underlined at rest, because colour cannot set them apart; on hover a 2px rule draws in from the left. Links that leave the site carry a small arrow.
links.sentence: A link inside running text looks like <link>this one</link>.

segmented.note: One control for language, theme, test length and axis picker: equal segments and an inverted indicator that slides between them. Arrow keys move the selection.

modes.note: Each mode is one link across the whole row. On hover the row wipes to inverted, START slides in and the arrow rolls (pinned on Quick in the light frame). Deep is dashed and not clickable yet.

matrix.title: Button state matrix
matrix.lead: Every variant, size and state, with hover and press pinned. Switch the control style to compare sharp, pill and offset.

home.lead: Home page variant for design review.

screens.title: App screens
screens.lead: Designed now, built in their phases: the test screen (Phase 3) and the result poster, which doubles as the share card.
screens.legend: Bar: score · hatched band: likely range

test.openLeft: {count, plural, one {# question is still open.} other {# questions are still open.}}
test.goToOpen: Go to the first open one
test.allDone: Every question has an answer or a skip.
test.notStored: This browser does not allow local storage, so your answers last only until you close the tab.
test.englishOnly: The statements are in English for now; translations follow.

results.title: Your results
results.lead: Read from this browser only; nothing about your result is in the address bar or on a server.
results.empty: There is no result in this browser yet. Results are stored on this device only, so a result from another browser will not show here.
results.notStored: This browser does not allow local storage, so this result disappears when you close the tab.
results.lowQuality: Your answers follow a pattern that makes this reading less reliable (see “How sure this is”). Treat it as a rough sketch.
results.atrocityNote: This ideology is tied to mass atrocities. A match describes positions on the twelve axes, not support for what was done in its name.
results.inBetween: You sit between {a} and {b}: the two are almost equally close.
results.honest: Percentages are similarity on twelve axes, spread out on purpose: 100% would mean identical positions. This is an interpretation, not a measurement of who you are.
results.unusualBody: Only {percent}% of the ideologies in the catalog sit within 15 points of you here.
results.typicalBody: {percent}% of the ideologies in the catalog sit within 15 points of you here.
results.indexFormula: Index = {formula}, scaled to ±100 · explains {share}% of the catalog's variance in this category
results.placementLow: Placement of this entry is uncertain.
results.axesLead: Each bar runs from the first pole (−100) to the second (+100). The hatched band is the likely range: wider when your answers on that axis were few or pulled in different directions.
results.radarHow: The centre is −100 on every axis, the solid inner ring 0, the outer ring +100. Your profile is the solid, hatched shape; the dashed outline is your closest ideology.
results.indicesLead: Each index summarises the three axes of a category with weights learned from the catalog (its first principal component). Where one number would hide too much, the three axes are shown instead.
results.matchesLead: Ranked among {count} ideologies in the catalog. Variants are grouped under their parent ideology.
results.moreCatalogs: Countries, historical regimes, figures and parties join the matches as their catalogs are built.
results.overallBody: {percent}% across the twelve axes, from {answered} answers and {skipped} skips. Skips are never counted as neutral.
results.tensionsBody: Your answers pulled in different directions on: {axes}. Those scores sit near the middle of a wider range.
results.tensionsNone: No axis where your answers pulled clearly apart.

placementBody.high: {name} is placed with high confidence in the catalog.
placementBody.medium: {name} is placed with medium confidence; its sources differ on some axes.
placementBody.low: {name} is placed with low confidence, so it never leads the summary when another match is about as close.

flags.acquiescence: Answers leaned towards agreeing whatever the statement said.
flags.contradiction: Some paired statements were answered in opposite directions.

results.shareLead: Sharing creates a short link with your twelve rounded scores and confidences, never your answers. Until you press the button, no link exists.
results.more: {count} more questions sharpen this result, and your answers so far are kept.

pilot.title: Help test the questions
pilot.intro: Thank you for helping. You take the normal test; at the end your browser saves one small answers file.
pilot.contains: The file contains your answer to each question (or a skip), how long each answer took, the test length, the language and, if you add it, a country code. It contains no name, no date and no information about your device.
pilot.sensitive: Political views are sensitive personal data. Please take part only if you are comfortable with that.
pilot.nothingStored: Nothing is sent to or stored on any server, and this page uses no cookies: your answers exist only on this page until the file is saved, then they are cleared.
pilot.yourChoice: You decide whether to pass the file on, and to whom.
pilot.noSwitch: Please do not change the language or reload during the test: the answers live only on this page.
pilot.countryHint: Two letters, e.g. CH, DE, GB. Leave it empty if you prefer.
pilot.countryError: Error: use two letters, such as CH.
pilot.consent: I understand what the file contains and that it holds my political views.
pilot.banner: Pilot: answers stay on this page and become a file at the end.
pilot.saved: Your answers were saved as {name}. Pass it on only if you want to.
pilot.cleared: The answers have been cleared from this page.
